mainTopic: Are עבדים treated like קרקע or like מטלטלין, for collecting debts from יתומים and for acquiring them together with other property?
overview: After רב נחמן leaves, עולא reveals that רבי אלעזר allowed a creditor to collect slaves even from orphans, which treats slaves like land. רב נחמן disagrees strongly and orders courts that ruled this way to return the slaves. When רבא challenges him, רב נחמן cites אבימי's ברייתא showing that slaves are not like land for פרוזבול or for acquiring movables along with them. The גמרא then suggests that two ברייתות argue about this very question. רב איקא בריה דרב אמי answers that the ברייתות agree. In one version slaves are like land, but movables need land that does not move, like the 'fortified cities in Judea'. In the other version slaves are like movables, and items on the slave are acquired with him. That leads to the 'walking courtyard' problem, and the גמרא rules that this works only when the slave is tied up. A new ברייתא says acquiring land acquires the slaves, and the גמרא answers that the slaves were standing on the land. The גמרא then finds that this 'standing on the land' condition is hard to explain under both versions of רב איקא.

steps.title: עולא reveals רבי אלעזר's full view after רב נחמן leaves
steps.stepSummary: Once רב נחמן has left, עולא tells the others that רבי אלעזר said a creditor can collect slaves even from the debtor's orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, עולא said to them: This is what רבי אלעזר said: even from orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא waits until רב נחמן is gone, then shares the fuller version of רבי אלעזר's ruling: a creditor may take slaves as payment even from orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a creditor can collect from orphans only from land, because land carries a שעבוד (lien), while movable things do not. Saying 'even from orphans' means רבי אלעזר treats slaves like land for this purpose. עולא had not said this part openly in front of רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Treating slaves like land means they can be collected from heirs. This sets up the whole dispute that follows.

phrases.english: After he went out,
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן, who was talking with עולא just before this.

phrases.english: Ulla said to them,
this is what Rabbi Elazar said:
even from orphans.
phrases.notes: He means a creditor can take slaves as payment even from the heirs who inherited them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier conversation between עולא and רב נחמן and gives the fuller version of רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, slaves may be collected for a debt even from the debtor's orphans, like land.

steps.title: רב נחמן: עולא dodged me
steps.stepSummary: When רב נחמן hears what עולא said, he complains that עולא avoided telling him the full ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: עולא evaded me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reacts to עולא's statement. He says עולא slipped away from him by not stating the full view to his face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן disagrees with treating slaves like land. His complaint suggests he would have argued against the ruling if עולא had said it in front of him.

keyTerms.meaning: he slipped away from me / evaded me

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Ulla evaded me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן's reaction to עולא's report in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן objects that עולא kept the full ruling from him, which shows he does not accept it.

steps.title: Two courts actually collected slaves from orphans
steps.stepSummary: The judges of נהרדעא and רב חנא בר ביזנא in פומבדיתא each ruled that a creditor could collect slaves from orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in נהרדעא, and the judges of נהרדעא collected. There was a case in פומבדיתא, and רב חנא בר ביזנא collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of two real cases in which courts followed רבי אלעזר's view. In both, they let creditors take slaves from orphans. This sets up רב נחמן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stories show that the view in step 1 was put into practice, not just discussed in theory. Two separate courts ruled that slaves count like land.

keyTerms.meaning: they collected (they had the debt paid)

phrases.english: There was an incident in Neharde'a,
and the judges of Neharde'a collected.
phrases.notes: The text leaves it unsaid, but they collected slaves that the orphans had inherited.

phrases.english: There was an incident in Pumbedita,
and Rav Chana bar Bizna collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows courts that ruled according to the view עולא reported in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courts ruled in practice that slaves may be collected from orphans.

steps.title: רב נחמן orders the slaves returned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells those judges to give the slaves back, or he will make them pay out of their own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: Go return them. And if not, we will collect it from your mansions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן strongly rejects those rulings. He orders the judges to undo them and threatens to make them pay personally if they refuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that slaves are like movable property, so they cannot be collected from orphans at all. He treats the judges' ruling as such a clear mistake that the judges themselves must fix the loss.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the judges stole. He means their ruling was a clear error, so they are responsible to make up the orphans' loss.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
Go and return [it],
phrases.notes: Return the slaves to the orphans.

phrases.english: and if not –
we will collect from you, from your mansions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן: זִילוּ אַהֲדוּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן's response to the court rulings described in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves may not be collected from orphans. Judges who ruled otherwise must reverse it or pay.

steps.title: רבא: so many authorities disagree with you, whom do you follow?
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists עולא, רבי אלעזר, the judges of נהרדעא and רב חנא בר ביזנא, and asks רב נחמן what his view is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: There is עולא, there is רבי אלעזר, there are the judges of נהרדעא, and there is רב חנא בר ביזנא. Whom does the master follow?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן. Everyone mentioned so far treats slaves like land, so what is רב נחמן's source for ruling against them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge. רבא is stacking up four authorities against רב נחמן and demanding his basis.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
There is Ulla, there is Rabbi Elazar,
there are the judges of Neharde'a,
and there is Rav Chana bar Bizna;
the master – in accordance with whom does he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: הָא עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's order in step 4 by pointing to all the authorities who disagree.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that slaves are not like land and cannot be collected from orphans.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Four authorities, both teachers and practicing courts, treat slaves like land. רב נחמן seems to stand alone without a source.

steps.title: רב נחמן's source: אבימי's ברייתא about פרוזבול and acquiring movables
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites a ברייתא taught by אבימי. A פרוזבול works on land but not on slaves, and movables can be acquired along with land but not along with slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I know a ברייתא, as אבימי teaches: A פרוזבול takes effect on land but does not take effect on slaves. Movable property is acquired together with land, but is not acquired together with slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא with a ברייתא. In two areas of הלכה, slaves do not get the status of land, and he uses that to support his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרוזבול protects a debt from שמיטה only if the borrower owns land, and owning slaves does not count. Movables can be acquired together with land in one act of קנין, but not together with slaves. Both rules show slaves are not treated like land, which supports רב נחמן's ruling about collecting from orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
a document that keeps a loan from being cancelled by שמיטה

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that slaves are like movable property, not land. His proof is אבימי's ברייתא: slaves do not count as land for פרוזבול, and movables cannot be acquired 'together with' slaves the way they can with land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the larger question of whether slaves have the status of land or of movables, which the sugya keeps working through.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I know a baraita –
as Avimi teaches:
A prosbol takes effect on land,
but it does not take effect on slaves.
Movable property is acquired together with land,
but it is not acquired together with slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 5 by giving a source for רב נחמן's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that slaves are not like land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אבימי: a פרוזבול does not work on slaves, and movables are not acquired together with slaves.

steps.title: Suggesting a dispute between תנאים: the first ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question of slaves' status is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא that treats slaves differently from land: taking hold of slaves does not acquire movables sold together with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between תנאים. One ברייתא teaches: If someone sold slaves and land together, and the buyer took possession of the slaves, he did not acquire the land. If he took possession of the land, he did not acquire the slaves. If he sold land and movables, and the buyer took possession of the land, he also acquired the movables. If he took possession of the movables, he did not acquire the land. If he sold slaves and movables, and the buyer took possession of the slaves, he did not acquire the movables. If he took possession of the movables, he did not acquire the slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the argument between רב נחמן and the others is really an older argument between תנאים. It starts by quoting the first ברייתא, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is the last case. Land can carry movables along with it, but in this ברייתא slaves cannot. So this ברייתא seems to treat slaves like movables, just as אבימי's ברייתא did.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים
Took possession, by an act of ownership such as using or working the item

steps.confusionAlert: Focus on the last case, slaves and movables. That is the case the second ברייתא will contradict. The earlier cases are just background.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים –
phrases.notes: The "it" is the question from the earlier steps: are slaves treated like land or not?

phrases.english: If he sold him slaves and land;
if he took possession of the slaves – he did not acquire the land,
if he took possession of the land – he did not acquire the slaves.
If he sold land and movables;
if he took possession of the land – he acquired the movables,
if he took possession of the movables – he did not acquire the land.
If he sold slaves and movables;
if he took possession of the slaves – he did not acquire the movables,
if he took possession of the movables – he did not acquire the slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן's proof from אבימי, the גמרא suggests the same disagreement already exists among the תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a tannaitic opinion treating slaves like movables, not like land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that taking possession of slaves does not acquire the movables sold with them.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא which rules that taking possession of slaves does acquire the movables sold with them. This clashes with the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in another ברייתא: If he took possession of the slaves, he acquired the movables!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a second ברייתא that directly contradicts the last ruling of the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, slaves could not carry movables along with them. Here they can, which is exactly how land works. So the two ברייתות give opposite rulings in the same case.

phrases.english: But it was taught: if he took possession of the slaves –
he acquired the movables!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that contradicts the last ruling of the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the first ברייתא that taking possession of slaves does not acquire movables.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings in the very same case, so they cannot both be right as they stand.

steps.title: The two ברייתות argue about whether slaves are like land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the two ברייתות disagree on one basic point. One holds slaves are like land, and the other holds slaves are like movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about this: one master holds slaves are like land, and the other master holds slaves are like movables?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the contradiction by suggesting the two ברייתות hold different views on the status of slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא lets slaves carry movables along, the way land does, so it holds slaves are like land. The first ברייתא does not, so it holds slaves are like movables. If this is right, רב נחמן and the others are simply each following a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (proposes an explanation)

steps.whyThisMatters: If the dispute goes back to the תנאים, then רב נחמן's position has tannaitic support, and so does the opposing position of עולא and the others.
steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion is that the two ברייתות are an argument about one question: are slaves like land or like movables?

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they disagree –
that one master holds: slaves are like land,
and the other master holds: slaves are like movables?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the contradiction between the two ברייתות as a real dispute about the status of slaves.
steps.raayaObject: That whether slaves are like land is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two contradicting ברייתות about acquiring movables along with slaves.

steps.title: Everyone agrees slaves are like land, but movables need land that does not move
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בריה דרב אמי says both ברייתות hold that slaves are like land. The ברייתא that says 'he does not acquire' requires land like the 'fortified cities in Judea,' which never move, and slaves do move.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא son of רב אמי said: Everyone agrees that slaves are like land. The ברייתא that says the buyer does acquire the movables is easy to understand. The ברייתא that says he does not acquire them holds that we need land like the 'fortified cities in Judea,' which do not move. Slaves walk around, so they do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 9's idea that the two ברייתות argue. רב איקא says both agree slaves are like land, and explains the 'does not acquire' ruling a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the ברייתות disagree about what slaves basically are. רב איקא keeps slaves in the category of land for both of them. The 'does not acquire' ruling is an exception: buying movables along with land only works with land that stays in place, and a slave can walk away.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone; all opinions agree
Fortified cities in Judea, from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: רב איקא does NOT say slaves stop being like land. He says they are like land, but this one rule (buying movables along with land) needs land that does not move.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said:
According to everyone, slaves are like land.
And that which is taught, 'he acquires,' is fine;
and that which is taught, 'he does not acquire':

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵינַן קַרְקַע דֻּומְיָא דְּ״עָרִים מְצוּרוֹת בִּיהוּדָה״ –
phrases.english: we require land similar to 'fortified cities in Judea,'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 21:3. The next lines show why this פסוק matters.

phrases.english: which do not move.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 9's claim that the ברייתות argue about the basic status of slaves.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the two ברייתות are a מחלוקת תנאים about whether slaves are like land.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'does not acquire' ruling can be explained by an extra requirement (non-moving land), not by a disagreement about the category of slaves.

steps.title: The משנה: movables are acquired along with land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: property without a guarantee (movables) is acquired together with property that has a guarantee (land), through money, a document, or חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: property that does not serve as a guarantee (movables) can be acquired together with property that does serve as a guarantee (land), through money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the basic rule that movables can be bought along with land. This sets up the next question: where does this rule come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land is called 'property with a guarantee' because a lender can collect from it. Movables are 'property without a guarantee.' The משנה says one act of acquiring the land also covers the movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Property without a guarantee, meaning movables
Property with a guarantee, meaning land
A document, here a bill of sale
Taking possession by an act of ownership

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Property that does not serve as a guarantee
phrases.notes: Movable things, which a lender can't collect from once they're sold.

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee,
through money, a document, or taking possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the rule behind רב איקא's reference to 'fortified cities in Judea.'
steps.raayaObject: The rule that movables can be acquired along with land.

steps.title: The source: gifts given with the fortified cities
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. חזקיה cites a פסוק where a father gave gifts of silver and gold together with fortified cities in Judea.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this? חזקיה said: the פסוק says, 'And their father gave them great gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, with fortified cities in Judea.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule comes from a פסוק about cities. This explains why the 'does not acquire' ברייתא wants land like cities, land that stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'with' (עם) shows the movable gifts were given together with the cities. Since the model case is fixed cities, one ברייתא requires land that does not move. That is how רב איקא's first answer works.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn these things?

steps.whatToRemember: In רב איקא's first version, slaves are like land, but movables are only acquired with land like the 'fortified cities': land that does not move.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
Ḥizkiyya said: As the verse states:
'And their father gave them great gifts,
of silver, and of gold, and of precious things,
with fortified cities in Judea.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה in Step 11, completing רב איקא's first answer.
steps.raayaObject: That acquiring movables along with land is modeled on fixed, non-moving land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 21:3, as explained by חזקיה

steps.title: Second version: everyone agrees slaves are like movables
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב איקא: both ברייתות hold slaves are like movables. The 'he acquires' ברייתא is talking about items the slave is still holding.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב איקא son of רב אמי said this instead: Everyone agrees slaves are like movables. The ברייתא that says 'he does not acquire' is easy to understand. The ברייתא that says 'he acquires' is talking about a case where the items are still on the slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב איקא's answer. It still says the ברייתות agree, but this time slaves are like movables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'does not acquire' ruling is the simple one, since you cannot buy movables along with other movables. The 'he acquires' ruling is the exception: the items were on the slave, so acquiring the slave pulls in what he is holding.

keyTerms.meaning: While they are still on him

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same רב איקא, just a different report of what he said. The two versions take opposite views of what slaves are, but both say the ברייתות do not argue.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said:
According to everyone, slaves are like movable property.
And that which is taught, 'he does not acquire,' is fine;
that which is taught, 'he acquires,' is when they are still upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא – עַבְדֵי כְּמִטַּלְטְלִין דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רב איקא's rejection of Step 9, opposite to Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Again rejects the claim that the ברייתות are a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'he acquires' ruling can be limited to a special case (items on the slave) instead of showing slaves are like land.

steps.title: A slave is a walking courtyard, which cannot acquire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version. A slave is at most a 'walking courtyard,' and a walking courtyard does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even if the items are on the slave, what difference does it make? He is a walking courtyard, and a walking courtyard does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the slave's holding the items lets the buyer acquire them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person's courtyard acquires things placed in it for him. But a slave walks around, so he is a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard cannot acquire. So 'still on him' should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
Courtyard, which can acquire items for its owner

phrases.english: But even if they are still upon him, what of it?
It is a walking courtyard,
and a walking courtyard does not acquire!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case of 'still on him' from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that items on the slave are acquired along with him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave is a moving courtyard, and a moving courtyard cannot acquire items placed on it.

steps.title: Standing still does not help: רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer. Even if the slave is standing, רבא said that whatever cannot acquire while moving also cannot acquire while standing or sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say this is when the slave is standing still, didn't רבא say: anything that does not acquire when it is moving also does not acquire when it is standing or sitting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off an escape route for the second version: limiting the case to a slave standing still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could try to say the slave is not moving at that moment, so he is not a 'walking courtyard.' רבא's rule says the status depends on what the thing is, not on whether it is moving right now. Since a slave can walk, he never acquires as a courtyard.
steps.whatToRemember: The second version of רב איקא is now under strong attack. A slave counts as a walking courtyard even when he is standing still, so items on him should not be acquired.

phrases.english: And if you would say it is where he is standing,
but didn't Rava say:
Anything that, if it were moving, would not acquire,
does not acquire when standing or sitting!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בְּעוֹמֵד, וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens Step 14's challenge by blocking the answer of a standing slave.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense that the slave was standing still when the items were acquired.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's rule: anything that cannot acquire while moving cannot acquire while standing or sitting either.

steps.title: The הלכה: a tied-up slave works like a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a slave can acquire items for his master as a 'courtyard' only when he is tied up and cannot move.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: when the slave is tied up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gets out of the problem from steps 14-15 by ruling that the ברייתא saying 'he acquires' is talking about a slave who is tied up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said that something that cannot acquire while moving also cannot acquire while standing still. A tied-up slave is different, because he cannot move at all. That makes him like a regular courtyard that stays in place, so the items on him are acquired by his master.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה (the practical ruling) is
Tied up, bound so he cannot move
A courtyard, meaning property that acquires items placed in it for its owner

steps.whatToRemember: A slave counts as a 'courtyard' for his master only when he is tied up. A slave who can walk is a 'walking courtyard' and does not acquire, even while he is standing or sitting.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with standing still. רבא already said that standing or sitting does not help (step 15). Only being tied up and truly unable to move makes the slave work like a courtyard.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: where he is tied up.
phrases.notes: The slave is tied up and can't walk away, so the things on him are acquired by his master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in steps 14-15 by limiting the case to a slave who is tied up.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A bound slave is like a stationary courtyard and acquires for his master. A slave who can move does not.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says acquiring land acquires the slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says taking possession of land also acquires the slaves, which contradicts the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: if he took possession of the land, he acquires the slaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new contradiction. The first ברייתא said acquiring land does not acquire slaves, but this ברייתא says it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא treats slaves as separate from the land, so acquiring the land does not bring the slaves with it. This new ברייתא says the opposite: a חזקה on the land is enough to acquire the slaves too. The two sources seem to clash head-on.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If he took possession of the land,
he acquires the slaves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the slave-as-courtyard issue to a new contradiction about acquiring slaves together with land.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's ruling that taking possession of land does not acquire the slaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא explicitly rules that taking possession of land does acquire the slaves, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: The slaves were standing on the land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא saying 'he acquires' is talking about slaves who are standing inside the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is when they are standing within it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that says 'he acquires the slaves' is talking about slaves who are physically standing on the land being acquired. Because they are inside it, they are acquired together with the land.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other source

phrases.english: There, it is where they are standing within it.
phrases.notes: "There" means the ברייתא just quoted, which says he acquires. "It" means the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is talking about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to disagree about whether acquiring land acquires slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that says the slaves are acquired is talking about slaves standing on the land.

steps.title: So the first ברייתא means slaves not on the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference that the first ברייתא's 'he does not acquire' must be talking about slaves who are not standing on the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, this 'he does not acquire' is when they are not standing within it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what step 18's answer implies about the first ברייתא. It is setting up the next move, where this inference will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'he acquires' is about slaves on the land, then 'he does not acquire' must be about slaves who are not on the land. The גמרא is not settled yet. Next it checks whether making the difference depend on 'standing on the land' fits each of the two versions of רב איקא's teaching (Steps 20–22).

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from this it follows

phrases.english: By implication, that this "he does not acquire"
is when they are not standing within it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the answer in step 18 means for the first ברייתא, preparing a further challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the first ברייתא's ruling 'he does not acquire' must now be limited to slaves who are not standing on the land, and whether that reading holds up.

steps.title: The answer works well if a slave is like movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that the answer from Step 18 (the slaves are standing on the land) fits well with the version of רב איקא בריה דרב אמי that says an עבד is like מטלטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works out well according to the version where רב איקא son of רב אמי said that a slave is like movable property. That explains why, if the slaves are standing on the land, yes, they are acquired, and if not, no, they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. First it shows that the answer from Step 18 fits one version of רב איקא's teaching, and next it will ask about the other version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of what רב איקא said: an עבד is like מטלטלין, or an עבד is like קרקע. If an עבד is like מטלטלין, then it makes sense that he is acquired along with the land only when he is physically on it. So the difference between the two ברייתות (standing on the land or not) fits this version.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (sets up a 'but according to the other view' challenge)
Version, or way of reporting a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: 'הניחא' is not a final ruling. It is only the first half of a pattern: 'this works for view A, but for view B there is a problem.'

phrases.english: This works out well according to that version

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: in which Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said:
A slave is like movable property;
that is why, if they are standing within it (the land), yes, they are acquired,
if not, no, they are not acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer from Steps 18–19 against the second version of רב איקא's teaching (the איכא דאמרי in Step 13, that an עבד is like מטלטלין) and finds that it fits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If an עבד is like מטלטלין, it makes sense that he is acquired along with the land only when he is standing on it.

steps.title: Problem if a slave is like land: שמואל's ten fields
steps.stepSummary: If an עבד is like קרקע, why must he stand on the land? שמואל taught that taking possession of one field acquires all the fields sold together, even ones in other countries.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the version that says a slave is like land, why do I need the slaves to be standing on the land? Didn't שמואל say: if someone sold him ten fields in ten countries, once he takes possession of one of them, he acquires all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 18 using the other version of רב איקא's teaching, the one where an עבד is like קרקע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל teaches that land does not need to be physically connected: a חזקה on one field acquires every field in the same sale, even far away. If slaves are like land, they should be acquired the same way, wherever they are standing. So the condition 'standing on the land' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Took possession (a חזקה, an act of acquiring land)

steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule shows that land can be acquired as one group no matter where each piece is, which makes the 'standing on it' condition hard to explain if slaves count as land.

phrases.english: But according to that version which said:
A slave is like land;
why do I need them to be standing within it?
Didn't שמואל say:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר לוֹ עֶשֶׂר שָׂדוֹת בְּעֶשֶׂר מְדִינוֹת,
phrases.english: If he sold him ten fields in ten countries,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהֶחְזִיק בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן – קָנָה כּוּלָּן!
phrases.english: once he took possession of one of them, he acquired all of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הניחא…אלא pattern from Step 20 by raising the problem for the other version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 18 (slaves are acquired with the land only when standing on it), according to the version that an עבד is like קרקע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that land is acquired as a group even when the pieces are far apart. If slaves are like land, they should be acquired with the land even when they are not standing on it.

steps.title: Counter-challenge: even if a slave is like movable property, why must he stand on the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even according to the version that an עבד is like מטלטלין, why should standing on the land be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, according to the version that says a slave is like movable property, why do I need him to be standing on the land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around (ליטעמיך) and says the 'standing on the land' condition is hard to explain even according to the version that seemed to fit in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 assumed that movable property is acquired together with land only when it sits on the land. This step questions that assumption: the challenger holds that מטלטלין can be acquired along with land even when they are not on it. If so, the answer from Step 18 fits neither version.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (turns the question back)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not defend the 'slave is like land' version. It shows that the 'standing on the land' condition is a problem for both versions, so the answer from Step 18 itself is now in doubt.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
according to that version which said:
A slave is like movable property;
why do I need him to be standing within it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts Step 20's claim that the answer fits the 'movable property' version, so the problem from Step 21 applies to both versions.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 20's assumption that movable property must be on the land to be acquired along with it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מטלטלין can be acquired along with land even when they are not on it, then the 'standing on the land' condition is unnecessary under the movable-property version too.
